# --- ast.py: add HasVar + constant folding in Predicate
path='ast.py'; src=open(path).read()
anchor = "class HasMatch(NodeVisitor):"
hasvar = '''class HasVar(NodeVisitor):
    """Determines whether an expression reads any (lexical) variable."""

    def visit_Var(self, node): return True
    def visit_Const(self, node): return False
    def visit_Match(self, node): return self.visit(node.expr)
    def visit_Not(self, node): return self.visit(node.expr)
    def visit_Field(self, node): return self.visit(node.expr)
    def visit_Index(self, node): return self.visit(node.expr)

    def visit_Binop(self, node):
        # Boolean operators short circuit, so only the branches that can
        # actually be reached matter; check both to stay conservative.
        return self.visit(node.left) or self.visit(node.right)

    def visit_Forall(self, node):
        return self.visit(node.array_expr) or self.visit(node.body or node)


'''
assert anchor in src
src = src.replace(anchor, hasvar + anchor, 1)

old_pred = '''class Predicate(object):
    """A compiled predicate: an expression plus its environment holder."""

    __slots__ = ('expr', 'holder', 'closure')

    def __init__(self, expr, environment=None):
        self.expr = expr
        self.holder = [environment if environment is not None else {}]
        self.closure = None if expr is None else compile_closure(expr, self.holder)

    def evaluate(self, environment=None):
        if self.closure is None:
            return True
        if environment is not None:
            self.holder[0] = environment
        return bool(self.closure())
'''
new_pred = '''class Predicate(object):
    """A compiled predicate: an expression plus its environment holder.

    An expression that reads no variable at all has the same truth value for
    every record, so it is folded once here instead of being replayed for each
    of potentially thousands of guards and runs.
    """

    __slots__ = ('expr', 'holder', 'closure', 'constant')

    def __init__(self, expr, environment=None):
        self.expr = expr
        self.holder = [environment if environment is not None else {}]
        self.constant = None
        if expr is None:
            self.closure = None
            return
        if HasVar().visit(expr):
            self.closure = compile_closure(expr, self.holder)
        else:
            value = bool(Evaluator({}).visit(expr))
            self.constant = value
            self.closure = None

    def evaluate(self, environment=None):
        closure = self.closure
        if closure is None:
            return True if self.constant is None else self.constant
        if environment is not None:
            self.holder[0] = environment
        return bool(closure())
'''
assert old_pred in src

new = '''def canonical_text(value):
    """Canonical JSON text of a recovered value.

    Serialisation preserves exactly the identity the corpus needs: booleans
    stay distinct from integers, empty arrays stay distinct from empty
    objects, and object key order is normalised.  It is also orders of
    magnitude cheaper than a recursive Python walk over large aggregates.
    """
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False,
                      separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False)


def corpus_key(entry, inputs):
    """The corpus identity of one recovered record."""
    return (entry, canonical_text(inputs))
